title: The Sum of All Values

concept.title: The same pattern, with a different combination
body: The sum of all values of a tree is the value of the root plus the sum of the left subtree plus the sum of the right subtree. The empty tree has sum 0. It is the same shape as counting the nodes: only the number added for the root changes from `1` to `root.val`.

Values can be negative, and a tree can have 20000 nodes with values up to 10^9 in absolute value, so the sum can reach 2 * 10^13: it needs a 64-bit integer in C++ (`long long`) and Java (`long`). In Python integers never overflow.

statement: Print the sum of the values of all nodes of a binary tree.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
hints: The empty tree has the sum 0.
Add the value of the root to the sums of the two subtrees.
Use a 64-bit type for the sum.

        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1

explanation: The sum of an empty tree is 0; otherwise it is the root value plus the sums of the left and the right subtree.

        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.

    i = 1

        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:

        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
